stories.title: Overnight wind cluster rakes Illinois, Indiana and Kentucky with 100+ damage reports
stories.summary: SPC storm reports for July 26 log more than 100 severe wind reports and 8 hail reports, concentrated in Illinois, Indiana and Kentucky, with zero tornadoes. Measured and estimated gusts reached 70 mph at Vincennes, IN and Earlington, KY; Uniontown, KY reported roughly 50% of Union County without power, and Nebraska saw trees snapped 12 to 18 inches in diameter near Clarkson.
stories.angle: A wide wind swath means a surge of roof and siding files across three states at once. Fast, documented eyes-on-roof inspections give adjusters decision-ready wind findings while the damage is fresh and dated.

stories.title: Severe weather rolls on: Wisconsin under warnings this morning, Great Lakes at risk Monday
stories.summary: As of mid-morning July 27, NWS severe thunderstorm warnings covered multiple Wisconsin counties with 60 mph gusts and quarter-to-half-dollar hail, under a severe thunderstorm watch running to 3:00 PM CDT. Forecasters kept a damaging-wind and hail threat over the upper Midwest and Great Lakes into Monday.
stories.angle: Back-to-back severe days stack new claims on top of yesterday's files. Carriers that line up inspection capacity now keep cycle times flat while volume spikes.

stories.title: Atlantic stays silent: NHC expects no tropical development for the next seven days
stories.summary: The National Hurricane Center's 8:00 AM EDT July 27 outlook shows no active systems and states tropical cyclone formation is not expected in the Atlantic, Caribbean or Gulf during the next 7 days.
stories.angle: A quiet tropical window is when carriers clear reinspection backlogs and lock in CAT-response capacity with inspection partners before the back half of the season.

stories.title: Aerial-imagery limits spread: Tennessee bulletin echoes Kentucky's, and analysts call it a national theme
stories.summary: Tennessee's Bulletin 25-03 warns that blurry, outdated or imprecise remote imagery cannot reasonably justify a property-claim denial, tying misuse to unfair claims practices, while Kentucky's Bulletin 2026-01 requires clarity, a written summary, and imagery date-stamped within 12 months. Legal analysts at Troutman Pepper Locke describe aerial-imagery limits as an emerging multi-state regulatory theme, with North Carolina also issuing guidance.
stories.angle: Regulators are saying imagery flags an issue but a validated inspection proves it. That validation step is exactly the documented, on-site work Hancock delivers for carriers and their adjusters.

stories.title: J.D. Power 2026: homeowners claims average 40 days from FNOL to final payment
stories.summary: The J.D. Power 2026 U.S. Property Claims Satisfaction Study puts the average homeowners claim at 40 days from first notice of loss to final payment, per an Insurance Journal Research whitepaper, which argues insurers can cut 16 days from the cycle without adding staff. The whitepaper itself is undated on the page.
stories.angle: Most cycle-time leakage is chasing missing information. An inspection file the adjuster can write an estimate from directly removes the chase and shortens every downstream step.

stories.title: North Carolina fraud crackdown: duplicate hail claims charged, roof-tampering sting caught on video
stories.summary: North Carolina DOI investigators charged a Raleigh couple with filing a $30,000 duplicate wind-and-hail claim for damage already settled with another insurer, per Claims Journal. Separately, a sting operation run with a regional carrier's special investigations unit filmed a roofing-company manager bending and ripping shingles to manufacture a $30,000 storm claim.
stories.angle: Fraud pressure raises the value of dated, photo-documented condition records. An independent inspection file that shows what the roof actually looked like, when, is the carrier's cleanest defense.

stories.title: Florida's SB 808 roof-inspection bill is dead — despite reports it takes effect July 1
stories.summary: Florida Senate records show SB 808, which would have expanded the list of authorized roof inspectors and barred nonrenewal based solely on roof age, died in committee on March 13, 2026 — yet multiple consumer articles still describe it as taking effect July 1, 2026. Existing law stands: past 15 years of roof age, insurers may require an inspection, and cannot deny solely on age if an authorized inspector certifies 5 more years of useful life.
stories.angle: Confusion about who may inspect and what the law requires lands on the adjuster's desk. Clear, code-literate inspection documentation helps carriers answer policyholders with the rule as it actually is.

stories.title: Roofing contractors pivot from storm-chasing to lifecycle relationships as margins tighten
stories.summary: An industry outlook citing ServiceTitan's 2026 market report says 75% of roofing and exterior contractors expect revenue growth this year even as margins compress, with the strongest operators building maintenance plans and standing commercial relationships rather than depending on storm-triggered demand.
stories.angle: The contractor side of the industry is drifting toward lifecycle service — the same direction Hancock positions with carriers: property lifecycle management, not one-off claim inspections.
